links.outcome: Reading grade level of original caregiver discharge documents versus recommended health literacy levels
links.effect: Original documents had mean FKGL 8.91 (SD 1.38), above recommended levels; 0 of 15 met FKGL 6 or below at baseline, 11 of 15 (73%) after AI simplification.
links.quote: Eleven of 15 documents (73%) achieved the target readability threshold of FKGL 6 or below, compared with zero at baseline.

links.outcome: Readability improvement and content integrity of AI-simplified discharge documents
links.effect: Mean FKGL fell 3.94 grade levels (8.91 to 4.97; P<0.001), but 35 flags occurred across 14 of 15 documents, including 12 safety-critical errors; 3 documents needed clinician revision.
links.quote: Content integrity review identified 35 flags across 14 of 15 documents: 12 safety-critical errors, 16 completeness gaps, and 7 accuracy concerns.

links.outcome: Safety-critical errors and omissions in AI-simplified discharge documents needing clinician review
links.effect: 12 safety-critical errors, 16 completeness gaps, 7 accuracy concerns across 14 of 15 documents; 3 documents had omissions requiring clinician revision before use.
links.quote: AI-assisted simplification should be implemented only with structured clinician review.

links.outcome: Errors and omissions in AI-generated simplified text that clinicians would need to verify
links.effect: 35 flags in 14 of 15 documents; larger word-count reduction correlated with more safety-critical flags (Spearman rho 0.63; P=0.012).
links.quote: Greater word-count reduction was associated with a higher burden of safety-critical flags (Spearman rho 0.63; P=0.012).

unlisted_practices: Prioritizing clinician review of AI-simplified documents by magnitude of word-count reduction

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the readability and clinical safety/content integrity of ChatGPT-simplified pediatric orthopaedic discharge documents using retrospective public documents. It does not test a specific deployment safeguard/practice against a control, though it concludes clinician review is needed.
